label: verify-bm-simulation-fem

claims.claim: Timoshenko coefficient and 3/2 ceiling at m=n^-0.5 reproduced: 1-D to 2.9e-15, 2-D plane-stress FEM to 1.2e-7 over n=1..50, and to 5e-5 at the optimum up to n=2000.
claims.source_says: max |f_numeric - f_closed| ... 2.887e-15; max |FEM/Timoshenko f - 1| = 1.160e-07 at n=10, m=0.05; n=2000 m=0.02236 f_FEM 1.50007, rel.err +4.98e-05
claims.note: All three numbers appear in the agent's own output files s01, s02 and s06; I read the output text and did not re-run the scripts.

claims.claim: Ceiling is 3/2 only for a free strip; plane strain reaches (1+nu1)*3/2: 1.95 at nu=0.30, 2.235 at nu=0.49; modulus ratio still drops out.
claims.source_says: largest FEM coefficient = 2.23500 at n=1, m=1 (ceiling 3/2 = 1.5; ratio 1.49000); case B largest 1.95000; f_FEM at optimum identical for n=1..50
claims.note: Matches the output file; this is the agent's own FEM result, verified only in 2-D plane strain, as the agent itself says.

claims.claim: In the 3-D linear model, curvature along the strip is width-independent (equal nu under 1e-4; mismatched 0.49/0.35 at most 0.32 percent low) and cross-width curvature is synclastic.
claims.note: Table rows agree; kz/kx is not meaningful below w/h=4, which the agent states elsewhere, so the synclastic statement holds for w/h>=4 only.

claims.claim: In the large-deflection model, length curvature is 1.4 percent below Timoshenko at w=h/sqrt(f*d_eps) and 13 percent below at twice that width (n=10 optimum, L/h=40), so narrower strips behave as the 1-D law.
claims.note: 1-0.986=1.4 percent and 1-0.866=13.4 percent reproduce; h/sqrt(1.5*0.01)=8.2h so lam is about 1 there; the result comes from one polynomial Ritz model, and the 'narrower behaves as 1-D' part is an extrapolation.

overall: All four key claims match the agent's own output files, and the arithmetic reproduces. The checks were against local result text, with no re-runs. They test the agent's own simulations, not a published source. The large-deflection claim rests on a single Ritz trial space (degree 4) and one aspect ratio.
